entries.name: University of Toronto — Accessibility Services
entries.description: Accessibility Services helps students navigate disability-related barriers to their academic success at U of T and provides services and supports for learning, problem solving and inclusion. Students register with the office to access academic, practicum or residence accommodations.
entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page; registration with the office is required for accommodations.
entries.address: 455 Spadina Avenue, 4th floor, Suite 400, Toronto, ON M5S 2G8
entries.evidence: Our team assists in navigating disability-related barriers to your academic success at U of T
entries.notes: Intake section names autism and attentional concerns among the areas supported. In-person visits and virtual appointments (phone or Microsoft Teams) are both offered.

entries.name: University of Toronto — Access Us Peer Mentorship Program
entries.description: Students are paired with an Access Us peer mentor, an upper-year student who is also registered with Accessibility Services, and join a community with social events and leadership, professional and career development. Open to undergraduate and graduate students who are new to Accessibility Services or new to U of T.
entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page.
entries.evidence: You will connect with an upper-year student who is also registered with Accessibility Services
entries.notes: Disability-focused peer mentoring run by Accessibility Services; not specific to neurodivergent students.

entries.name: University of Toronto — Centre for Learning Strategy Support
entries.description: The Centre for Learning Strategy Support guides U of T students in developing effective learning and study strategies, skills and competencies. Its programs include online and in-person offerings.
entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page.
entries.address: 800 Bay Street, 5th floor, Toronto, ON M5S 3A9
entries.evidence: We help you identify and achieve your learning goals.

entries.name: University of Toronto — Student Life Events
entries.description: Student Life's events page points U of T students to ways of keeping up with Student Life events, activities and programs, including listings on Folio and Facebook.
entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page.
entries.evidence: There are SO many cool things going on in Student Life.
entries.notes: The page itself does not list events; it links out to the listings.

entries.name: University of Toronto — Social Association for Students with ASD (SASA)
entries.description: An Accessibility Services social group described as a dedicated space exclusively for students diagnosed with or who self-identify as having Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD); one event is held in person and the other online. The same Social Groups page lists ASD Peer Connections for Women & Trans Students, where no formal diagnosis is required.
entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page.
entries.evidence: a dedicated space exclusively for students diagnosed with or who self-identify as having Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
entries.notes: Autism-specific. Open to undergraduate and graduate students registered with Accessibility Services or who identify as living with ASD.

entries.name: University of Toronto — ADHD Skills Group
entries.description: A facilitated learning community for students with ADHD who are registered with Accessibility Services, where students develop strategies to manage challenges and harness their strengths. Participants commit to all sessions and to developing an action plan.
entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page.
entries.evidence: The ADHD Skills Group is a facilitated learning community for students with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)
entries.notes: ADHD-specific. The page lists a named staff facilitator as the contact; students are referred by their accessibility advisor.

entries.name: McGill University — Student Accessibility & Achievement
entries.description: Student Accessibility & Achievement serves students experiencing academic or physical barriers who have a documented disability, mental health condition, chronic health condition or other impairment. Appointments, exam scheduling and forms are handled through its online portal, ClockWork.
entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page.
entries.address: 1010 Sherbrooke Street West, Suite 410, Montreal, Quebec H3A 2R7
entries.evidence: Empowering students to reach their academic potential by widening access to learning.
entries.notes: The office also runs McGill's Tutor Matching Program and a Peer Mentor Program for registered students (separate entries).

entries.name: McGill University — New Student Buddy Program
entries.description: Campus Life & Engagement's New Student Buddy Program matches new students with a trained, upper-year mentor for advice on navigating university life and accessing campus resources. The same page lists faculty, department and group mentorship programs.
entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page.
entries.evidence: Get matched with a trained, upper-year mentor.
entries.notes: Listed on the page as open to all students.

entries.name: McGill University — Peer Mentor Program (Student Accessibility & Achievement)
entries.description: A peer mentoring program for students registered with Student Accessibility & Achievement, in which both mentor and mentee have active academic accommodation plans. Pairs are matched on academic background, extracurricular interests and individual preferences, and often meet weekly.
entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page.
entries.evidence: In this Peer Mentor Program, both mentor and mentee are students who have active academic accommodations plans
entries.notes: Disability-focused; not specific to neurodivergent students.

entries.name: McGill University — Tutor Matching Program
entries.description: Run by Student Accessibility & Achievement, the program matches requests for tutoring in any McGill course with qualified peer tutors. Some groups, such as newly admitted first-year undergraduates, can receive subsidized sessions.
entries.cost_note: $18.00 per hour for undergraduate tutors and $22.00 per hour for graduate tutors; subsidies for some groups.
entries.evidence: The Tutor Matching Program matches requests for tutoring (for any McGill courses) with qualified peer tutors.

entries.name: McGill University — Campus Life & Engagement Events
entries.description: Campus Life & Engagement events for McGill students are listed in myFuture (login required) while the office's website calendar is being rebuilt.
entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page.
entries.evidence: Campus Life & Engagement events are now hosted in myFuture.
entries.notes: The page says the full events calendar will return to the website in the Fall 2026 semester.

entries.name: McGill University — Neurodivergent and Chronic Conditions Student Support Group
entries.description: A Student Wellness Hub support group for neurodivergent students and students living with chronic conditions, focused on alternative learning methods and building confidence and communication skills, including with professors and teaching aides. Groups meet weekly for 10 weeks, are limited to 8 participants, and require a referral from a Hub professional.
entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page.
entries.evidence: This is a support group for neurodivergent students and students living with chronic conditions
entries.notes: Neurodivergent-specific. The newest listing found is a session dated 5 November 2025; earlier terms ran as the Neurodivergent Students Support Group. Current-term dates were not confirmed (Hub events now sit in myFuture). The page says it does not offer ADHD/ASD assessments or diagnoses.

entries.name: University of British Columbia — Centre for Accessibility

entries.address: Room 3110, Brock Commons South, 6180 Walter Gage Road, Vancouver, BC
entries.evidence: designed to remove barriers for students with disabilities and ongoing medical conditions
entries.notes: UBC Vancouver. Online services through Clockwork for Vancouver students.

entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page.
entries.evidence: UBC Hub of Ten Thousand Coffees is a platform available to all students.
entries.notes: Mostly alumni and professional mentoring; peer mentoring is listed for Computer Science and Integrated Sciences undergraduates.

entries.name: University of British Columbia — Chapman Learning Commons Tutoring & Advice
entries.description: The Chapman Learning Commons points students to tutoring offered in a variety of subjects through its campus partners, along with study advice.
entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page.
entries.address: Room 300, Irving K. Barber Learning Centre, 1961 East Mall, Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z1
entries.evidence: Tutoring is offered in a variety of subjects through our campus partners.

entries.name: University of British Columbia — UBC Events

entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page.
entries.evidence: Your source for events happening at UBC.

entries.name: University of British Columbia — ADHD Skills Support Group
entries.description: An in-person, non-clinical, non-diagnostic skills-based support group run through UBC Counselling Services for students who have ADHD or think they might have it. An ADHD diagnosis is not required; students register online through the booking portal.
entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page.
entries.evidence: If you have ADHD or think you might have ADHD, this in-person skills-based support group may be what you are looking for.
entries.notes: ADHD-specific. The page lists Wednesdays from Sep 9 to Oct 21, 2026, 3:00 to 4:30 pm, UBC Vancouver campus.

entries.name: University of Alberta — Accessibility + Accommodations
entries.description: Accessibility + Accommodations provides accommodation support to remove barriers for eligible students, with offices on North Campus, Augustana Campus and Campus Saint-Jean. Students manage academic accommodations through the online Accommodate application.
entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page.

entries.evidence: accommodation support is available to remove barriers for eligible students
entries.notes: Augustana Campus (780-679-1132, augpass@ualberta.ca) and Campus Saint-Jean (admiacad@ualberta.ca) contacts are also on the page.

entries.name: University of Alberta — Career Mentoring Program
entries.description: Career Education matches U of A students and graduates with mentors who act as informal coaches, role models and advisors to help them explore career options. The program runs once per academic year over four to six months, virtually or in person.
entries.cost_note: $75 program fee for mentees, payable after mentor matching.
entries.evidence: Mentors act as informal coaches, role models, and advisors, helping mentees explore career options
entries.notes: Mentors are not necessarily students. For peer connection, U of A's Unitea program (Student Success & Experience) offers free one-to-one and group tea times with trained Peer Hosts and Alumni Hosts.

entries.name: University of Alberta — Writing and Learning Centre
entries.description: Professional specialists and peer tutors offer workshops and personalized support with academic writing, study skills and time management for undergraduate and graduate students.
entries.cost_note: Appointments and workshops are free for current U of A students.
entries.address: 2-10 Cameron Library, Edmonton, Alberta T6G 2J8
entries.evidence: Our appointments and workshops are free for current U of A students.

entries.name: University of Alberta — Events
entries.description: The U of A events page lists events and important dates; the university hosts lectures, workshops, conferences and concerts throughout the year.
entries.cost_note: Varies by event; the page says students attend Golden Bears and Pandas games for free.
entries.evidence: Check here often for events and important dates!

entries.evidence: Dedicated to supporting students with disabilities through academic accommodations and related support.

entries.name: University of Waterloo — AccessAbility Services

entries.description: A directory of mentorship programs run by departments across the university, including Peer Leaders in Living Learning Communities for first-year students, Peer Success Coaching for all students, and the AccessAbility Peer Mentorship Transition Program for students registered with AccessAbility Services.
entries.cost_note: Cost not stated on the page.
entries.evidence: Departments across the university provide a number of programs that support Waterloo students

entries.name: University of Waterloo — Tutoring
entries.description: Lists tutoring options for Waterloo students: Tutor Connect for finding a Waterloo student tutor, and drop-in help from the Mathematics Tutoring Centre, Computer Science Consulting Centre, First-Year Engineering tutors and the Physics Tutorial Centre.
entries.cost_note: Free drop-in tutoring each term on the main campus; Tutor Connect rates are not stated.

entries.name: University of Waterloo — Waterloo Events

entries.cost_note: Varies by event.
entries.evidence: At Waterloo, we're proud to host a wide variety of events for the campus community and our larger community.
entries.notes: Student-specific listings are also at uwaterloo.ca/students/events.

entries.evidence: Whether you self-identify as neurodivergent or are exploring whether you might be, you are welcome here!
entries.notes: Neurodivergent-specific. Registration is through the Waterloo event portal linked on the page.

entries.evidence: Accessible Education provides supports and services to students with disabilities at Western, in all programs and faculties.

entries.name: Western University — Launch Peer Mentorship Program
entries.description: Western Launch's peer mentorship program supports students' transition to university by connecting them with upper-year student mentors from their faculty, with faculty-specific events and workshops and a drop-in Launch Lounge (UCC 270).

entries.address: Launch Lounge, UCC 270
entries.evidence: The Launch Peer Mentorship Program is here to support your transition to university
